title: Safety-windowed release velocity controller and health-driven throttles
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Build a release velocity controller that gates incremental traffic ramps inside finite safety windows and applies health-driven throttles (latency/error/quality) to prevent noisy slowdowns and cascade rollbacks. This ticket covers the control-plane changes (policy DSL + evaluator), a lightweight agent to enforce throttles at the edge, and the Console UX + dashboards to visualize velocity state. Motivation: previous incidents showed linear full-ramp strategies overshoot when a latent regression appears at 50% traffic; we need a conservative, observable default that enables predictable LTS promotions and reduces champion/promote flip-flop risk.
acceptance_criteria: Controller supports time-boxed 'safety windows' where ramp progress is capped by a configurable velocity_budget (tokens/min or pct-per-minute).
Health-driven throttle rules can be expressed using SLIs: p95_latency, error_rate, model_quality_regressions, and custom tags.
Auto-throttle reduces ramp rate and holds traffic when thresholds exceed configured limits; auto-rollback triggers only after sustained violation windows.
Console shows per-release velocity curve, current budget consumed, and per-cohort health signals; owners can pause/resume from Console.
End-to-end tests simulate a degraded cohort and demonstrate throttle prevents traffic overshoot and triggers expected alerts+rollbacks.
design_notes: Policy DSL: extend existing rollout policy to include 'safety_window{duration, budget, evaluation_interval}' and 'throttle{metric, threshold, decay}' primitives.

Enforcement: controller publishes target cohort weights to the traffic router; a short-lived enforcement agent at ingress rate-limits traffic growth to the target weight and can reduce it proactively when signaled.
Health signals: leverage existing telemetry (Console traces + metrics) and add a light-weight 'quality_regression' event emitted by eval pipeline to be consumed as an SLI.
Backpressure model: use exponential backoff on ramp steps when transient vs sustained violation (3 consecutive windows -> hard throttle).
Interaction with LTS: allow pinning rules that require manual approval for LTS promotions; velocity budgets for LTS channels default to conservative values.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary shadow): 0% => shadow traffic only; verify no hard regressions for 1h.
Phase 1 (initial canary): 1% -> hold in 15m safety window, must pass health checks to continue.
Phase 2 (paced ramp): automated +10% every 30m up to 50% using velocity_budget=10pct/hr, with throttle checks evaluated every 5m.
Phase 3 (broad rollout): slow ramp to 100% using lower budget for LTS channels; manual override required for >80% on LTS.
monitoring_runbook: Primary metrics: p99 latency, p95 latency, request_error_rate, quality_regression_rate, traffic_weight, velocity_budget_remaining.
SLO thresholds: p95_latency > 1200ms OR request_error_rate > 0.5% -> reduce ramp by 50% for one window; sustained for 3 windows -> hold and page.
Dashboards: new 'Release Velocity' dashboard linked at https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/release-velocity?release=ENG-53621.
Alerts: PagerDuty channel 'release-safety' on hold+page conditions; slack ephemeral alert in #releases with restart/handoff actions.
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy DSL parser and throttle evaluation logic.
Integration tests: simulate metric noise injection (latency spikes, error bursts) and assert controller reduces ramp and performs expected actions.
Chaos test: run simulated region network partition and ensure safety window prevents cascading promotion.
Canary rehearsal: run on staging with mirrored production traffic for 48h prior to first production run.
